## Responsive navbars, toolbars, and breadcrumbs

Translated labels and dynamic items can overflow a navbar at widths
where a fixed breakpoint does not trigger.
`watchInlineFit(host, row, onCompact)` toggles `data-fitting` to measure
the row’s natural width against the container. Wide and compact states
share one labelled `<nav>` element and its links
(`a[aria-current="page"]` marks the current page). Put `[navbar-toggle]`
on a disclosure button with `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` rather
than using an ARIA `menu`. Without JavaScript, the links remain visible
and wrap.

Use `[navbar]` with `[navbar-row]`, `[navbar-brand]`, `<nav>`,
`[navbar-toggle]`, and `[navbar-end]`. Optional modifiers are
`[navbar-align="center"]`, `[navbar-align="end"]`, `[navbar-vivid]`, and
`[navbar-sticky]`. `mountNavbar(host, {open, onOpenChange})` sets
`data-compact` when the row overflows and toggles `data-open` on the
`<nav>` row. `[navbar-brand]`, `[navbar-toggle]`, and `[navbar-end]`
stay on the first row while `<nav>` expands below them. `mountNavbar`
returns `{setOpen, dispose}` and closes the compact `<nav>` on Escape,
link clicks, or outside clicks. Call `mountNavbar` on a
`[navbar-sticky]` navbar even without `[navbar-toggle]`. It writes the
navbar’s height to `--navbar-size` on `:root` for
`scroll-padding-block-start` and removes `--navbar-size` on `dispose()`.

`[responsive-toolbar]` and `[breadcrumb]` use the same `data-compact`
and `data-fitting` attributes with their own compact markup and focus
handling. A `[responsive-toolbar]` contains `[toolbar-actions]`,
`[toolbar-group]`, `[toolbar-divider]`, `[toolbar-shortcut]`, and
`[toolbar-menu]`, switching from `[toolbar-actions]` to `[toolbar-menu]`
when compact. A `[breadcrumb]` contains `[breadcrumb-row]`,
`[breadcrumb-parents]`, `[breadcrumb-collapse]`,
`[breadcrumb-ancestor]`, and an ellipsized `[breadcrumb-current]`, with
spacing controlled by `--breadcrumb-gap` (default `--space-3`). When
compact, `[breadcrumb-collapse]` replaces `[breadcrumb-parents]`.

``` python
preview('''
<header navbar>
  <div navbar-row>
    <a navbar-brand href="#workspace">Workspace</a>
    <button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" navbar-toggle aria-controls="nav" aria-expanded="false">Navigation</button>

</header>
''', width='28rem', height='12rem',
```

## Dialogs, popovers, dropdowns, and tooltips

Use a native `<dialog dialog>` opened with `showModal()` for modal tasks
that block the page and trap focus until completed or cancelled.
Structured slots are `header` (`h2`, `p`), `[dialog-close]` in the
top-end corner, body `div` elements, and `footer`. Add
`[dialog-side="start"]` or `[dialog-side="end"]` to render a full-height
drawer whose width defaults to `--drawer-size` (`24rem`) and expands to
`100vw` below `40rem`.

Use native `popover="auto"` with `[popup]` or `[dropdown]` for non-modal
panels. Native popovers appear in the browser’s top layer without moving
the element out of its `[ui]` theme. A `[dropdown]` holds ordinary
links, buttons, and form inputs rather than an ARIA `menu`. Users move
through it with Tab and dismiss it with Escape or an outside click.
Inside `[dropdown]`, style entries with `[menu-item]` (supporting
`aria-pressed="true"`, `[ui-tone="danger"]`, and disabled states),
`[menu-label]`, `hr`, and `<details option-group>` for nested choices
instead of cascading flyouts.

On browsers with CSS `position-area`, `[popup]` and `[dropdown]` flip to
fit the viewport using `position-try-fallbacks`.
`mountPopover(trigger, panel, {onOpenChange, side, align, sideOffset})`
keeps `aria-expanded` in sync and calls `positionFloating`. On
supporting browsers, `positionFloating` sets `anchor-name`,
`position-anchor`, and `position-area`. On other engines, it computes
`left`, `top`, and `--floating-available-height` in JavaScript.
`mountPopover` hides the popover if the trigger scrolls out of the
viewport and returns a cleanup function. When the panel has
`[dropdown]`, it also focuses the first enabled item on open and closes
on link clicks.

Wrap a trigger and its `[role="tooltip"]` element in `[tooltip]`,
linking them with `aria-describedby`. CSS reveals the tooltip on
`:hover` or `:has(:focus-visible)` and delays hiding by `150ms` so the
pointer can cross into the tooltip. Set `--tooltip-gap` (default `6px`)
to adjust the offset. A tooltip never traps focus, does not close on
Escape, and requires no JavaScript.

``` python
preview(r'''
<div cluster>
  <button type="button" btn onclick="document.querySelector('#details').showModal()">Open dialog</button>
  <span tooltip>
    <button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" id="about" aria-describedby="tip" style="anchor-name: --about">About this workspace</button>
    <span role="tooltip" id="tip" style="position-anchor: --about">Shared with two coworkers</span>
  </span>
  <button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" id="actions" popovertarget="options">Options</button>
  <div dropdown popover="auto" id="options">
    <button menu-item type="button" popovertarget="options" popovertargetaction="hide">Rename workspace</button>
    <a menu-item href="#files">View files</a>
    <details option-group><summary>Preview type</summary>
      <button menu-item type="button" aria-pressed="true">Code</button><button menu-item type="button" aria-pressed="false">Note</button>
    </details>
  </div>
</div>
<dialog dialog id="details" aria-labelledby="title">
  <header><h2 id="title">Workspace details</h2></header>
  <p>Files and settings stay in the workspace.</p>
  <form method="dialog"><button btn>Close</button></form>
</dialog>
''', height='18rem', js=(assets/'floating.js').read_text() +
    r'''mountPopover(document.querySelector('#actions'), document.querySelector('#options'));''')
```

## Disclosures, tabs, toolbars, and toasts

Use `<details disclosure>` with `<summary>` for disclosures. Group
multiple `<details disclosure>` elements inside `[accordion]` with the
same `name` attribute when only one item should stay open at a time.

Mark tab structures with `[tabs]`, `[tablist]` (`role="tablist"`),
`[tab]` (`role="tab"`, `data-value`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`),
and `[tabpanel]` (`role="tabpanel"`, `hidden`).
`mountTabs(root, {activationMode, onValueChange})` handles arrow keys,
Home, End, and disabled tabs, returning `{setValue, dispose}`. In
`'automatic'` mode (the default), moving focus to a tab with arrow keys,
Home, or End selects it immediately. In `'manual'` mode, selection waits
for Enter, Space, or a click. Call `setValue(value)` to update selection
programmatically and `dispose()` to remove event handlers. For vertical
tabs, add both `[tabs-orientation="vertical"]` on `[tabs]` and
`aria-orientation="vertical"` on `[tablist]` to switch layout and arrow
keys to Up and Down.

`mountToolbar(root)` sets a single roving Tab stop on buttons and links
in a command row, with Left, Right, Home, and End traversal (respecting
RTL). It leaves elements inside `[popover]` dropdowns in normal Tab
order and returns a cleanup function. Application commands and
responsive collapsing stay outside `mountToolbar`.

`mountHoverPopover(trigger, panel, {openDelay, closeDelay})` opens a
popover on mouse hover after `openDelay` (default `0` ms). It closes the
popover after `closeDelay` (default `300` ms) once neither element has
hover or focus. Pressing `ArrowDown` on the trigger opens the panel and
focuses its first enabled item. Tapping on touch also opens the panel,
while the trigger’s click handler stays independent (for example, a
toggle button whose popover holds extra settings). `mountHoverPopover`
returns a cleanup function.

Use `[toaster]` and `[toast]` for transient feedback, and place urgent
messages during a modal task inside that modal. Keep the `[toaster]`
live region mounted in the DOM so new messages are announced.
`[toaster]` is fixed at the top-end corner by default, supports
`[popover]` top-layer rendering, and accepts
`[toaster-position="top-start"]`, `"bottom-start"`, or `"bottom-end"`.
CSS runs the `ui-toast-lifetime` animation on each `[toast]` (with
optional non-neutral `[ui-tone]`) for `--toast-duration` and pauses it
on `:hover` or `:focus-within`. Remove the toast from state or the DOM
when that animation ends.

``` python
preview(r'''
<div tabs tabs-orientation="vertical" id="preferences">
  <div tablist role="tablist" aria-label="Preferences" aria-orientation="vertical">
    <button tab type="button" role="tab" id="general-tab" data-value="general" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="general">General</button>
    <button tab type="button" role="tab" id="locked-tab" data-value="locked" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="locked" disabled>Team</button>
    <button tab type="button" role="tab" id="files-tab" data-value="files" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="files">Files</button>
  </div>
  <div tabpanel role="tabpanel" id="general" aria-labelledby="general-tab" tabindex="0">Use Up/Down to focus a tab, then Enter to select it.</div>
  <div tabpanel role="tabpanel" id="locked" aria-labelledby="locked-tab" hidden>Team settings</div>
  <div tabpanel role="tabpanel" id="files" aria-labelledby="files-tab" tabindex="0" hidden>Generated files stay in the workspace.</div>
</div>
''', height='12rem', js=(assets/'interactions.js').read_text() +
    r'''mountTabs(document.querySelector('#preferences'), {activationMode: 'manual'});''')
```

``` html
    <button tab type="button" role="tab" id="locked-tab" data-value="locked" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="locked" disabled>Team</button>
```
